description: Make cam journal append --cycle-close discoverable: document the flag and its exit-code contract in JOURNAL_HELP, add the exit-3 refuse-to-arm case to subagent-orchestrator.md (both copies plus embed), guard with a static help-text test. Doc and help text only, no runtime change.

userStories.title: Document --cycle-close and the exit-code contract in JOURNAL_HELP with a static help-text test
userStories.description: As a cam operator (or an agent grepping for the cycle-close mechanism), I need cam journal append --help to list --cycle-close and its exit-code contract so that the orchestrator-driven recycle arm is discoverable and the CAM-217 misdiagnosis (flag assumed nonexistent) cannot recur.
acceptanceCriteria: JOURNAL_HELP usage line lists --cycle-close alongside --force (for example: cam journal append [--force] [--cycle-close]). [oracle: bun index.ts journal --help | grep -q -- --cycle-close]

JOURNAL_HELP has an Options entry explaining that --cycle-close appends the cycle entry AND arms the orchestrator recycle marker, requiring the handoff file (.claude/.cam-orch-handoff.json) to be present and a live recycle watcher. [oracle: bun index.ts journal --help | grep -qi 'recycle marker']

JOURNAL_HELP documents the exit-code contract using the literal tokens 'exit 1', 'exit 3', 'exit 4': exit 1 (invalid or duplicate JSON), exit 3 (--cycle-close with the handoff file absent), exit 4 (--cycle-close with no live recycle watcher). [oracle: bun index.ts journal --help | grep -q 'exit 3' && bun index.ts journal --help | grep -q 'exit 4']

A static test extending test/commands/journal-append.test.ts asserts the journal --help output contains the --cycle-close token and the exit-3 and exit-4 mentions. [oracle: bun test test/commands/journal-append.test.ts]

No runtime behavior change: parseJournalArgs, the dispatchJournal arm logic, exit codes, recycle watcher, and context backstop are untouched; only the help-text string and the test file change. [oracle: bun test (the existing --cycle-close behavior tests at test/commands/journal-append.test.ts:592-730 pass unmodified)]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Full quality spine passes including biome lint (bun run check:all). [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: Files: index.ts (JOURNAL_HELP at lines 345-393: usage field at 348, Options section 359-367, Behaviour body already notes the exit-1 duplicate case at line 380; extend, do not restructure) and test/commands/journal-append.test.ts. Gotcha (root cause of CAM-217): the flag parse lives at index.ts:1258 (parseJournalArgs) and the arm block at index.ts:1367-1399 (dispatchJournal); src/commands/journal.ts is the pure appendJournalEntryOnMain library and legitimately has no flag, do not touch it or look for the flag there. Test pattern: follow the ISSUE_HELP block test at test/issue.test.ts:333 (intercept process.stdout.write, import main from ../../index.ts, run main(['bun','index.ts','journal','--help']), restore in finally); dispatchJournal's help path writes via process.stdout.write directly, not the injectable writeStdout, so interception is required. Consistency: the printFatalHint usage string at index.ts:1253 repeats the usage line; keep it in sync with the new usage text. Spec source: CAM-217 spec (settled at grill), doc and help text only.

Add the exit-3 case next to it: exit 3 means the handoff file .claude/.cam-orch-handoff.json is absent, i.e. step 1 (write the handoff) was skipped; recovery is write the handoff, then re-run cam journal append --cycle-close. Gotchas: dual-copy is per-file and not guaranteed byte-identical repo-wide (memory: cam-dual-copy-is-per-file), diff the two copies for this section before editing (currently identical here); edit BOTH copies then run bun run embed-vendor, and the embed-vendor:check gate applies.
